title: U.S. House · Virginia's 1st District
area: Virginia's 1st Congressional District (Northern Neck, Middle Peninsula, and parts of Fredericksburg-area and Hampton Roads exurbs)

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Robert J. Wittman advanced unopposed. Shannon Taylor won the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026 with 53.0% of the vote in a seven-candidate field.

summary.text: Robert J. Wittman is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Virginia's 1st District, first elected in a 2007 special election. He previously served on the Montross Town Council and as its mayor, on the Westmoreland County Board of Supervisors, and in the Virginia House of Delegates.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C. in 1959; earned a bachelor's degree in biology from Virginia Tech, a master's in health policy and administration from the University of North Carolina, and a Ph.D. in public policy and administration from Virginia Commonwealth University.
Worked as an environmental health specialist for local health departments and as field director for the Virginia Health Department's Division of Shellfish Sanitation.

Served on the Montross Town Council (1986-1996, mayor 1992-1996), the Westmoreland County Board of Supervisors (1996-2005, chair 2004-2005), and was elected to the Virginia House of Delegates in 2005.

positions.summary: Says on his official site that he supports ending catch and release and consistent enforcement of immigration laws, and that people with final removal orders should not be allowed to remain.
positions.quote: I support policies that restore order to our immigration system, end catch and release, and ensure our nation’s immigration laws are consistently enforced.

positions.summary: Says on his official site that continuing the enhanced ACA premium tax credits helps middle-income families, while Congress works toward broader reforms.
positions.quote: Continuing this assistance helps middle-income families keep more of their hard-earned money while Congress works toward broader reforms that lower health care costs and strengthen the individual insurance market.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources as Vice Chair, and on the House Committee on Armed Services, chairing the Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittee, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Serves on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Shannon Taylor
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 53.0% of the vote

summary.text: Shannon Taylor is the Commonwealth's Attorney for Henrico County and the Democratic nominee for Virginia's 1st District. She is campaigning on congressional ethics reform, including bans on stock trading and lobbying by members of Congress, alongside lowering costs for families.

background.text: Graduated from Albemarle High School; earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Virginia in 1989 and a law degree from the University of Richmond School of Law in 1995.
Has served as Commonwealth's Attorney (chief prosecutor) for Henrico County since 2012, saying her office secured a 90% homicide conviction rate.
Ran unsuccessfully for Virginia Attorney General in 2025, losing the Democratic primary to Jay Jones 51.1% to 48.9%.

priorities.text: Proposes mandatory jail time of at least one year for members of Congress who misuse at least $10,000 in taxpayer funds, and a lifetime ban on members of Congress becoming lobbyists for industries they regulated.
Proposes a ban on members of Congress trading individual stocks while in office and pledges to refuse corporate PAC contributions.
Says she will fight to restore expired Affordable Care Act subsidies and expand Medicare's ability to negotiate prescription drug prices.

positions.summary: Says she will fight to restore the Affordable Care Act subsidies and rural hospital funding, and to expand Medicare’s ability to negotiate drug prices.
positions.quote: I will fight to restore the Affordable Care Act subsidies that Rob Wittman allowed to expire and restore funding for rural hospitals.

positions.summary: Says she stands with a woman’s right to make choices about her own body and that she would never prosecute a woman for choosing an abortion.
positions.quote: I stand firmly with a woman’s right to make choices about her own body.

positions.summary: Says she will fight against tariffs, which she says are raising costs in the district and hurting farmers.
positions.quote: I will also fight against these tariffs and foreign wars that are raising costs across the district and hurting our farmers.
